customConcept.name: The French Laundry
customConcept.blurb: A stone farmhouse in Yountville, a tasting menu that changes daily, three Michelin stars and a waiting list of people who have planned their whole trip around one dinner.

setting.name: Washington Street, Yountville
setting.desc: A small, wealthy town in the middle of the Napa Valley, a few steps from other acclaimed restaurants and inns. Guests arrive from all over the world, many dressed for the one dinner of their lives; harvest season fills every inn in the valley.

ev.text: Harvest season in Napa: every inn in the valley is full and winemakers bring their best bottles to dinner.
Wildfire smoke settled over the valley for a week. Guests cancelled and the garden took a beating.

desk.title: A collector wants a private dinner
desk.text: A tech collector wants to buy out the whole restaurant for one night and bring his own verticals of Romanée-Conti. He's asking what it would cost.

choices.label: Quote the buyout
choices.blurb: A very good night, and the regular book shuffled.

ev.text: A viral post complained about the price of dinner, again. The waitlist didn't move.

log.text: You're the proprietor of The French Laundry in Yountville, three Michelin stars and one of the most famous restaurants in the world. The building is yours, the brigade is deep, and every night is judged.

mods.label: Property tax, the garden and the building

world.notes: This is The French Laundry in Yountville, in California's Napa Valley: a stone building from 1900 that was once a French steam laundry, with a culinary garden across the road, three Michelin stars, a daily-changing nine-course tasting menu at $425 a person as of January 2026 with service included (wine, supplements like truffle and caviar, and corkage extra), a jacket-required dress code, and reservations released months ahead. It was named the world's best restaurant in 2003 and 2004. Classic dishes include Oysters and Pearls and salmon cornets. In the real world it's Thomas Keller's restaurant; in this game you run it, and every staff name is invented. The wines by the glass and the trophy bottles, with their prices, are from the restaurant's published wine list (service included). Sales, seat count, cellar value and property value are estimates.

supplierPool.blurb: The culinary garden across the road, plus a handful of Napa and Sonoma growers picking to the kitchen's list.

supplierPool.name: East Coast oyster farm & day-boat fish
supplierPool.blurb: Oysters shipped overnight from New England and fish from boats that land the morning it's ordered.

supplierPool.name: Heritage ranches & A5 wagyu importer
supplierPool.blurb: Pastured lamb, squab and pork from small ranches, and Japanese wagyu with the paperwork to prove it.

supplierPool.name: Farmstead dairy & affineur
supplierPool.blurb: Cultured butter, cream and a cheese cave that ages the wheels for the cheese course.

supplierPool.name: Caviar, truffle & fine-foods house
supplierPool.blurb: White sturgeon caviar, Alba truffles in season, single-estate oils and vinegars.

dishes.name: Salmon Cornets
dishes.desc: A black sesame tuile rolled into a cone, piped with sweet red onion crème fraîche and topped with salmon tartare seasoned with chives, shallot and lemon oil.

dishes.name: "Oysters and Pearls"
dishes.desc: The opening course for decades: a warm "sabayon" of pearl tapioca with Island Creek oysters, finished with a spoonful of Regiis Ova caviar.
dishes.kitJ: "Oysters and Pearls"|The opening course for decades: a warm "sabayon" of pearl tapioca with Island Creek oysters, finished with a spoonful of Regiis Ova caviar.

dishes.name: Garden Spring Onion Medley
dishes.desc: Compressed Pink Rhône Little Gem lettuce with a sweet onion "panna cotta," marinated Aptos Farm kiwi and green garlic dressing, drawn from the restaurant's own garden.

dishes.name: Stonington Maine Sea Scallop "Poêlé"
dishes.desc: Seared Stonington scallop set on a Mount Shasta porcini "tapenade," with plancha-cooked Sweetheart Farms white asparagus, garden spinach leaves and whole grain mustard "béchamel."

menu.identity: Two nine-course tasting menus that change every day, one from the garden, built on classic French technique and the produce from across the road.

team.name: Julien Moreau-Hart
team.bio: Chef de cuisine. Came up through this kitchen's brigade and now runs it to the standard the house has held for thirty years.

team.name: Aiko Brennan
team.bio: Executive sous chef, the one who makes sure the thousandth plate of Oysters and Pearls looks like the first.

team.name: Tomás Lindqvist
team.bio: Sous chef running the garden-to-kitchen programme with the farm across the road.

team.name: Nadia Castellano
team.bio: Pastry chef responsible for the doughnuts, the mignardises and a laminated dough programme people fly in for.

team.name: Priya Haddad
team.bio: Wine director overseeing a cellar of many thousands of bottles and a list that runs to hundreds of pages.

team.name: Élodie Park
team.bio: General manager and maître d'. Knows who's celebrating what before they sit down.

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
